feature: Marketing Free Scan Review step (/scan/review) — Git #1374, Phase of Feature #1352. The Statement of Work generated from a Free Scan Prospect's own scan: eight numbered sections, a delivery-timeline Gantt, six phase-breakdown cards and a right rail carrying the scope selector, the payment-plan choice and the e-signature capture. Every figure is served by the real /api/public/free-scan/sow/* pair (routes/public-free-scan-sow.ts -> lib/free-scan-sow.ts), computed from the tenant's real buildPillarSummary output and the six real category='project' catalog rows. Nothing on the page is a fixture and no price is written into the .tsx.
notes: SCOPE OF THIS MANIFEST — what is deterministically assertable without a live consented tenant:
1. The identity gates on all five /api/public/free-scan/sow/* routes (apiTests). Every one of
them is unauthenticated on purpose (a Free Scan Prospect is never issued a JWT, #656) and
resolves the tenant only from a live checkout sessionId or an emailed fsr_ return token.
These assert the real refusal codes for a missing credential, a malformed sessionId, a
well-formed-but-unknown sessionId, and a bogus return token — the same guard shape
free-scan-page.json already locks for #1358/#1359's own routes.
2. That the Review page renders its flow strip with Review as the CURRENT step and
Consent/Scan/Results already ticked (uiSteps). This is the #1374 scope item 6 assertion and
it holds with no credential at all, because the strip renders above the document.
3. That a visitor with no free-scan session gets the honest 'we lost track of your scan' state
rather than an empty document or a crash.
WHAT IS NOT ASSERTED HERE, and why:
The document body itself (phase fees, finding counts, the 41 -> N projection, the Gantt) needs a
real consented tenant with a completed scan, which this environment cannot mint from a browser —
the consent grant happens in a popup on Microsoft's own domain. That half is covered instead by
artifacts/api-server/src/lib/free-scan-sow.live-db.test.ts, which seeds a scratch Prospect with a
real diagnostic run and real findings and asserts the whole computed document against live
Postgres (six phases really are catalog rows; the total really is the sum of their real fees;
deferring a phase really drops its fee, its findings and its Gantt bar and shortens the critical
path; a signed row cannot carry a partial signature block; a signed document is served from its
own snapshot rather than recomputed). Faking a consented session here to reach the document would
be coverage of a fixture, not of the product.
Stripe's own Payment Element is likewise not driven here — it is a cross-origin iframe, and the
charge path it fronts is the same metadata-bound intent/confirm handshake
public-purchase-payment.ts already uses.
